title: Auth token refresh and retries
summary: When the access token expires and many requests fail with 401 at the same time, refresh the token only once and replay them. Retry only safe failures, with growing delays.
body: **In simple words:** An access token is like a short-lived entry pass; a refresh token gets you a new pass. If 10 requests all find the pass expired, you want one trip to the counter, not 10.

**Single-flight refresh:** put an `actor` in front of the token. The first caller that needs a refresh starts a `Task` and saves it; everyone else awaits the same task. If refresh fails (refresh token revoked), log the user out once.
**Refresh early:** refresh a little before expiry so users rarely see a 401.

**Retries:** retry only transient failures (timeouts, connection lost, 5xx, 429) and only for requests that are safe to repeat (GET, or POST with an idempotency key). Never blindly retry a payment. Use exponential backoff with jitter (random delay) and respect `Retry-After`.
**Storage:** tokens in the Keychain, never in logs or UserDefaults.
**Login flows:** OAuth with `ASWebAuthenticationSession` + PKCE; passkeys (`ASAuthorization`) for passwordless sign-in; Sign in with Apple.
keyPoints: Actor + shared in-flight Task = one refresh for many concurrent 401s.
Retry only idempotent requests; backoff with jitter; honour Retry-After.
OAuth via ASWebAuthenticationSession + PKCE; passkeys for passwordless.

code.caption: Single-flight token refresh

mistakes: Every failed request triggering its own refresh (race, revoked tokens).
Retrying POST requests that create orders or payments.
followups: **How do you test the race?** Fire 10 concurrent requests with an expired token and assert the refresh endpoint was called once.
**What is jitter and why?** Randomness added to backoff delays so all clients do not retry at the same moment after an outage.
